Raden Ayu Tuti Marini Puspowardojo, commonly known as R.A. Habibie (19 November 1911 – 24 June 1990), was the mother of the 3rd president of Indonesia, B. J. Habibie. She was married to Alwi Abdul Jalil Habibie.
R.A. Habibie was known as a woman who frequently wore the kebaya yet was fluent in the Dutch language. She was described as having a dynamic mindset while remaining firm in practicing Javanese cultural traditions in her social life.
Biography
Intellectual traditions were instilled by Tuti's parents from an early age, alongside religious teachings and the traditional values held as ancestral heritage. While she was a student at the Hogere Burger School (HBS), Tuti met a young man from the Gorontalo people, specifically from the Kabila region of Gorontalo, named Alwi Abdul Jalil Habibie. At the time, he was a student at the Bogor Agricultural School.
The Alwi Habibie family carries the Habibie surname, an indigenous Gorontalo entity known for their expertise in coffee farming and livestock.
Marriage to Alwi Abdul Jalil Habibie
After completing his studies in Bogor, Alwi Abdul Jalil Habibie proposed to Tuti Marini Puspowardojo. They were subsequently married in a ceremony that incorporated both Gorontalo and Javanese customs, reflecting the cultural traditions of both families.
Shortly thereafter, Alwi Abdul Jalil was appointed as an agricultural expert in the Afdeling of Parepare, requiring Tuti Marini to leave her childhood memories in Yogyakarta. In Parepare, Tuti lived as a young mother and was blessed with nine children, though one (Satoto Muhammad Duhri Habibie) died at the age of one.
Rudy Habibie's Illness
When her son Rudy (B.J. Habibie) fell severely ill, the lack of local medical doctors led the family to seek help from a traditional healer, Raja Bau Djondjo Kalimullah Kara Engta Lembang Parang Arung Barru. After receiving water blessed by the Raja, Rudy's condition gradually improved.
A notable incident Tuti often recalled involved a Bugis belief prevalent in their community. Because Rudy's face closely resembled his father's, local tradition suggested he must be "sold" to prevent a misfortune—specifically the death of one of them or a long-term separation. Consequently, in a symbolic traditional ceremony, Rudy was "purchased" by the Raja of Barru with a keris.
Japanese Invasion of the Dutch East Indies
In 1942, news spread that Japanese imperial forces were entering Parepare. Tuti's family, along with other residents, were forced to abandon their home and possessions to evacuate to the village of Tete Aji.
Following the Dutch surrender to Japan, the family returned to Parepare, only to face Allied attacks shortly after. As the conflict intensified, Tuti and her family evacuated again to Landrai Village in the Mallusetasi district, located on the coastal road between Makassar and Parepare. They finally returned to Parepare after the Japanese defeat and the arrival of Australian troops.
Post-Independence and the Death of Alwi Habibie
In 1947, Tuti's husband was promoted to Head of Agriculture for Eastern Indonesia, based in Makassar. The family relocated there, reuniting with B.J. Habibie and his older siblings.
On 3 September 1950, while performing Isha prayers, Alwi Abdul Jalil Habibie suffered a fatal heart attack. Despite the family's efforts to seek immediate help, he died before medical assistance could arrive. At the time of his father's death, Rudy was in the second grade of the Concordante HBS.
Among her eight surviving children, two stood out for their achievements and character: Rudy and his younger brother Fanny (nickname for Junus Effendi Habibie). Despite their contrasting personalities, both showed extraordinary potential compared to their peers. Tuti endeavored to treat all her children fairly, though her pride in Rudy was particularly profound.
Move to Bandung
Despite increasing economic challenges, Tuti Marini remained hopeful for her children's future. She decided to move to Bandung to provide Rudy with a better education. Rudy initially attended HBS but transferred to SMP Negeri 5 and later other schools before passing the entrance exam for the University of Indonesia in Bandung (now the Bandung Institute of Technology), specializing in aeronautics. Tuti Marini eventually intended to send Rudy to Germany for his studies using her own funds, eventually securing government permission to purchase foreign exchange.
In July 1959, Tuti received word that B.J. Habibie was hospitalized in Germany with a severe influenza infection affecting his heart. She traveled to Germany to support him, helping him regain his spirit and health. Rudy eventually graduated as a top-tier engineer. Tuti lived to see the success of her children, fulfilling the promise she had made to her late husband.
Preservation of Javanese-Gorontalo Traditions
Tuti dedicated herself to raising her children to be healthy, agile, and disciplined, while introducing them to the Javanese culture and Gorontalo customs that formed her and her husband's cultural identity. She insisted that all her children marry using both Gorontalo and Javanese traditions as a mark of respect for their ancestral heritage. This included B.J. Habibie, who observed Gorontalo traditional customs during his wedding reception at the Hotel Preanger in Bandung.
Death
At the age of 78, Tuti Marini underwent heart bypass surgery and was treated for nearly two months at Mount Elizabeth Hospital in Singapore. She died in Bandung on 24 June 1990, surrounded by her eight children. Her body was flown to Jakarta and buried at the Tanah Kusir Cemetery, beside her husband, whose remains had been moved there from Ujung Pandang.
Personal life
From her marriage to Alwi Abdul Jalil Habibie, Tuti Marini had nine children:
* Titi Sri Sulaksmi Habibie Mantofani (28 December 1928 — 5 February 2016); married Maj. Gen. Subono Mantofani and had five children, including music promoter Adrie Subono.
* Satoto Muhammad Duhri Habibie (deceased in infancy).
* Alwini Karsum Habibie (born 1933).
* Bacharuddin Jusuf "Rudy" Habibie (25 June 1936 — 11 September 2019), who served as the third President of Indonesia; married Hasri Ainun Besari (11 August 1937 — 22 May 2010) and had two children.
* Junus Effendi "Fanny" Habibie (11 June 1937 — 12 March 2012); married Meike Mariam Supardi Habibie (5 March 1937 — 28 February 2008) and had three children.
* Sri Redjeki Chasanah Habibie Darmosoewito (8 October 1938 – 2 November 2017); married Maj. Gen. Soedarsono Darmosoewito (1927 — 2005) and had four children.
* Sri Rahayu Fatimah Habibie Muchdar (14 December 1941 – 15 November 2024); married Muchsin Mochdar.
* Ali Buntarman Habibie (1945 — 1946).
* Suyatim Abdurrahman "Timmy" Habibie (9 November 1950 – 21 January 2024).
In popular culture
* In the film Habibie & Ainun (2012), Tuti Marini Puspowardojo is portrayed by Ratna Riantiarno.
* In the film Rudy Habibie (2016), Tuti Marini Puspowardojo is portrayed by Dian Nitami.
